# Gyblos Explorer

> Live, public metrics of the Gyblos peer-to-peer AI inference network on Solana: which sellers are online, which models they serve and at what price, their uptime, how many requests the network served, and what Gyblos payment channels settled on chain.

Gyblos is an open market where anyone can sell, buy or give away AI inference. The explorer at https://explorer.gyblos.com shows the network as it is, from public sources only. It is on Solana devnet during the beta; mainnet is planned for 2026-12-09.

## How to read the figures

- Free and paid usage are always shown as a pair ("free · paid") and never added together: free volume is not backed by payment.
- Usage comes from signed receipts that sellers and buyers report to the metrics collector. The request count includes requests only the seller reported; requests both sides reported are matched first.
- Buyer counts below 5 are withheld and shown as "< 5", never as zero.
- Amounts are USDC, computed from exact atomic units. Times are UTC.
- "Gyblos" channel figures come from payment channels whose opening transaction carries a Gyblos memo. That label is self-declared by whoever opens the channel.
- A ✓ next to a seller means the discovery index checked that the named GitHub account published the seller's NodeId in a gist; it links the seller to that account, does not identify a person and says nothing about quality. Sellers without it are not marked. Online sellers with at least 7 days of history come first, by whole-percent 7-day uptime and then by lowest paid output price; newer sellers follow, by price. `?verified=1` shows only verified sellers, online or not.
- A seller is online when it has a live signed presence in the discovery index, offline when it was seen before but has none now, and not published when it was never seen or withdrew its catalog.
- Channel transactions list the latest instructions of Gyblos payment channels on chain (channels whose open carries a Gyblos memo or whose distribute pays the Gyblos treasury), all time and newest first, not filtered by the range; `?before=<cursor>` pages to older ones. Each amount is per row (the buyer deposit, newly settled, what the seller side received, or what went back to the buyer) and must not be added up; only Paid out is shown as money (green), deposits and refunds are muted with their direction; a payout row also lists the rest of its split: the Gyblos fee, the payments program (the payment program's own treasury: rounding remainders, or a share it could not deliver; not a Gyblos fee), what went back to the buyer and any unclassified remainder; a split shared by several channels is the transaction's batch total, shown on its first paying row, and the transaction's other paying rows say they are part of that payout. When the metrics collector does not send the split (an older collector), payout rows show no amount rather than the whole vault outflow. The seller is shown when the channel's payout recipient equals the owner address of exactly one listed seller; that owner is self-declared, so it is a display hint, not proof. A listed seller links to its page; a payout shared by several channels says "Several channels"; otherwise the row says "Unlisted seller".
- Each seller has a page at `/sellers/<NodeId>` (64 lowercase hex characters; anything else is a 404, and so is a NodeId that a whole, current read of the index does not know and that the collector has no activity for in the last 90 days; with a source down or dated, the page renders and is not indexed): its identicon, self-chosen name (not verified) when it set one, verified GitHub account, NodeId and self-declared owner address; its online, offline or not-published state with its online-since or last-seen time (and the time of the index read when it is dated), 24 h and 7 d uptime (only while it is listed); its requests, success rate, output tokens and seller first-token p50 over the range (free · paid), the paid usage both sides authorized, how many models it served ("100+" at the collector's cap of 100 models), free and paid requests-per-day charts, a model table (context and prices of its current offer; requests, success and first-token p50 over the range) and a daily table with buyer counts (below 5 shown as "< 5"); and the channel transactions whose payout recipient is its owner address, all time, newest first, with the same amounts, split lines and colours as the main list (a batch total when a transaction paid several channels, which may include other sellers' channels). The owner address is published only while the seller is online, so an offline seller's page lists no transactions. There is no earned total: the collector has no per-seller on-chain total yet. Its tables use the same parameters as the main page (`modelsPage`, `dailyPage`, `before` with `txPage`), and its links keep `range` and `verified`.
- The page shows the last 7, 30 or 90 days (`?range=7`, `?range=30`, `?range=90`); 30 is the default.
- Every table shows 25 rows per page, with its page in its own parameter: `sellersPage` (Sellers, after the verified filter and ordering), `offlinePage` (Not online), `modelsPage` (Models), `dailyPage` (Usage daily), `demandPage` (Unserved demand), `chainDailyPage` (Daily on chain) and `txPage` (Channel transactions, numbered alongside its `before` cursor). A missing, invalid or out-of-range page is dropped from the URL and shows page 1 (while a table's source answers only in part, an out-of-range page shows page 1 but stays in the URL), and every page link keeps the other parameters. A range switch returns Models, Usage daily, Unserved demand and Daily on chain to page 1; the other tables keep their page.
- Each seller links to its own page at `/sellers/<NodeId>`; the ✓ links to the GitHub proof gist.

## Public data sources

- [Discovery index](https://discovery.gyblos.com/v1/models): models offered now; `/v1/sellers?model=<id>` lists live sellers, `/v1/uptime?node=<NodeId>` a seller's uptime, and `/v1/network` every registered seller's online, offline or not-published state.
- [Metrics collector](https://collector.gyblos.com/v1/stats/network): daily network totals; `/v1/stats/models` per model and `/v1/stats/chain` on-chain settlements. Each takes `from` and `to` as `YYYY-MM-DD`, at most 92 days. `/v1/stats/sellers/<NodeId>` one seller's daily and per-model totals. `/v1/stats/chain/txs` lists Gyblos channel transactions, newest first, paged with `before` and `limit`, and `recipient=<address>` keeps only channels whose first payout recipient is that address (a payout's split then sits on the first matching row, with the whole transaction's values).
